title: SMB2: Add a fid subtree to SMB2 commands
description:
The trees are shown in the 10 SMB2 requests and response types
and include the following info:

    Filename: <filename>
        File Id: <FID>
        File Id Hash: <hash>
        Frame handle opened: <frame #>
        Frame handle closed: <frame #>

notes.body: This is not my commit (not what I pushed). It belongs to someone else! Please assist.

?

What help do you need ?
What does "git status" say?

Hi, it says "nothing to commit, working tree clean".  This all started when

smb2_add_a_fid_tree_to_all_cmd_types --force" which required me to
authenticate by popping up username and password dialog boxes. Of course
that didn't work because I believe we now need to authenticate with SHA but
I had no idea how. Can you help?  Note that I would be happy to have the
entire commit tree deleted and start over with a new branch name with just
HEAD.

can you squash change ? and git push -f ?

Instead of squashing the 7 commits I deleted the six oldest ones in an interactive rebase. Then I pushed it with a --force. My local commit history looks clean. I no longer see the 6 unwanted commits locally or on the remote but I can't get it to run my change through the pipeline. Unless you can help me resolve that, I would be happy to close the merge request, delete the branch entirely (-D), and start over again clean. What do you suggest?
Yes, it is the better solution i think...

Hi Alexis. I deleted the branch locally (-D) but couldn't do so on the remote. I created an entirely new branch locally and it appears to have placed it as a branch of my first branch! I need the WS admin to handle this. Can You please give me his/her address? I appreciate any help you can offer.
You need to set a new branch name
resolved all threads

That's exactly what I did. I created a branch name that I had never used before. However illogical, I believe the key here is that Gitlab did not allow me to delete the branch I had -D deleted on my local system. Presumably, this was due to a lack of permissions. Attaching a new branch to my existing branch on the remote makes no sense because we can work on multiple changes at the same time on different branches on the remote just like we do locally. That is why I need to speak to the admin. I'd rather not bother Gerald with this. Am I missing something?
I do not know git very well but I think your fork is all in your hands nothing anyone else can do...
Anders how can I contact the admin?

You are the admin of your fork as far as I understand.
Is this helpful?
https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/user/project/repository/branches/

It says "No one can delete a protected branch using Git commands, however, users with at least Maintainer role can delete a protected branch from the UI or API." I don't believe I am a maintainer because it won't let me delete my branch. I may try to get help from GitLab support. The key reason for wanting to delete it is because it refuses to run the pipeline and does not explain why it won't.

The reason for failed builds is the number of extra development commits in the history. I was able to condense them down to one commit following:

1. Update to the latest master branch and rebase your changes _on top_ of it. Right now you created an undesired new "merge commit" which is the other way round.
```
git fetch https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark.git master:master
git rebase master
```

2. Perform an interactive rebase, changing all but the first `pick` line to `s` (squash).
3. After closing the commits editor, it will open an editor with the combination of all commit messages. Delete all except the last commit message.

If you have difficulties with this, I can also try this and overwrite your branch. Let me know if you need any more help!

Peter, thanks for your help.
When I ran your first command with my master checked out I got the error: "fatal: refusing to fetch into branch 'refs/heads/master' checked out at 'C:/ws-dev/wireshark'" Then I updated my master in the usual manner (git pull --rebase upstream master), and tried your command again with the same result. 

My default branch on the remote is "smb2_add_a_fid_tree_to_all_cmd_types"
I deleted this branch on my local with a -D some time ago. Should I recreate that branch name on my local, update it to the latest master, make changes, push it, and create a new merge request?

My guess is that you need to download the branch again if you wish to continue on this MR and this branch.

Otherwise I'd start over by deleting the MR creating a new branch/MR with a new name and continue from there. You might want to backup your code changes first.

In general it is better to have one commit per MR and amend that commit as you go. Small commits probably gets reviewed faster as well.

That branch no longer exists on my local machine because it was deleted
